clue.text: On-screen image a match official gathers in case of argument

indicators.note: to gather something is to take it in, so one piece encloses another
a case is the outside shell, so only the outermost letters of the next word count

blocks.note: taken as written
VAR is the video assistant referee in football
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A referee clutching a video still while settling a dispute on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The video assistant referee is a recent addition to football officiating; 'case' reads as a legal case but means the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An avatar is the figure or picture representing a user on a computer screen or in a game.

clue.text: Instrument I brought down — there it is!

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing a letter down moves it lower in the column, so it is reinserted further along

blocks.note: a stringed instrument slightly larger than a violin
the letter itself, which is moved

explanation.surface: A musician pointing triumphantly at the instrument just carried downstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I of VIOLA and move it one place lower: VIOLA becomes VOILA.
explanation.definitionFit: Voilà is the French exclamation, borrowed into English, used when presenting something: here it is.

clue.text: Historian translated 17th-century chronicler's absorbing article

indicators.note: something absorbing soaks another thing up, holding it within

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for translated
John Evelyn, the 17th-century English diarist
the indefinite article

explanation.walkthrough: 'Translated' looks like an anagram signal but is simply the abbreviation TR.
explanation.definitionFit: G. M. Trevelyan was a leading English historian of the twentieth century, as was his great-uncle Macaulay.

clue.text: Fine! I will tuck into fishy food for a starter

indicators.note: to tuck into food is to eat it, so these pieces go inside the dish

blocks.note: OK, an expression of agreement
taken as written
fish eggs eaten as food

explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' poses as a first course at dinner; it is a person starting out.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a newcomer or beginner, someone just starting out in a job or sport.

clue.text: Maybe record written by past Labour leader in March

explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot led Britain's Labour Party in the early 1980s and was known for marching at CND rallies; his record is FOOT'S LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: To footslog is to trudge or march a long way on foot, a verb meaning to march.

clue.text: Santa Fe charms artist travelling astride horse

horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.walkthrough: 'Santa Fe' reads as the US city, but the clue splits after Santa, which is the definition. Horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H.

clue.text: Issue clergyman raised, given nothing initially for extra work

says the piece for nothing is placed at the very start of the answer

short for Reverend

explanation.definitionFit: Overtime is work done beyond normal hours, or the payment for it, so it is extra work.

clue.text: Party held by certain people briefly in wicked place

clue.text: Tick off job, changing frame of upper entrance

first and last letters of the word

clue.text: This may keep a red grouse, we hear, dry in part of tree

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word is matched by its sound

clue.text: Where Japanese train departs and heads for Osaka, journeying onwards

initial letters of the three words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' reads as a railway train, but it is a verb: where the Japanese practise.
explanation.definitionFit: A dojo is a hall or school where Japanese martial arts such as judo and karate are practised.

clue.text: Range of products for keeping plants in jelly

explanation.walkthrough: The clue splits after 'in', which reads as ending 'keeping plants in'; it is the link to the definition.

clue.text: Quality of a sound medic, cutting fag out

explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the tone colour that distinguishes one voice or instrument from another, a quality of sound.

clue.text: Carry out gong character used twice in symphony

the only letter appearing twice in the word

explanation.walkthrough: A gong is British slang for a medal or honour, such as the OBE (Order of the British Empire).
explanation.definitionFit: To obey an order is to carry it out as instructed, so the two verbs match.

clue.text: Part of the head tribesman's ground

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Cambrian is an adjective meaning Welsh, from Cambria, the Latin name for Wales.

clue.text: Diet European fed to fertile male

standard abbreviation

clue.text: Escapist fiction writer right behind Catholic Church

CE, the Church of England
standard abbreviation

clue.text: You can't possibly miss this dratted churl, according to Spooner

explanation.walkthrough: Barn door is the proverbial target too big to miss, as in 'couldn't hit a barn door'.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn door is the standard example of a target so large that no one could miss it.

clue.text: More pleasant but nameless kitchen decorator?

explanation.definitionFit: An icer puts icing on cakes, so in a playful sense they decorate things in the kitchen.

clue.text: It's used to film live reels in the can before noon

first letter of the word
